changes.before: Implement Counter with private #value, constructor(initial), add(amount), read(), and static zero(). Each zero() call returns a distinct instance at0. Inputs are finite numbers; add mutates only its receiver and returns its new value.
changes.after: Keep a counter's value private and create fresh counters from the class.

before: #value is a private field declared in the class body. Methods of this class access it as this.#value. It is not the same as a public property named "#value", and outside code cannot directly write first.#value. This is language-level encapsulation, not encryption or a promise that an object can safely hold secrets against all program code.

static zero() is called on Counter, not on an instance. It takes no arguments and returns a fresh Counter initialized to 0. Each constructor call creates separate private state. add(amount) adds the supplied finite number and returns the updated value; read() returns the current value with no mutation.
after:
A field beginning with `#` is private to the class that declares it. Methods in `Counter` can use `this.#value`.

Outside code cannot directly read or write that private field. This controls access through JavaScript code; it does not encrypt the value.

A static method belongs to the class. Call `Counter.zero()`, not `first.zero()`.

Our `zero` method makes a new counter starting at zero. Each counter has its own saved value. `add(amount)` changes that counter and returns its new value. `read()` returns the value without changing it.
